caption: A lightning bolt forks into two branches before reaching the ground, both branches lighting up together.

sa.check: A lightning bolt descends from the sky toward the ground.
The bolt forks into two branches before reaching the ground.
The two branches share one trunk above the fork.
The branches appear at the same moment, not one after the other.

pc.expect: The bolt is a jagged bright line with a single trunk from the cloud that splits at one point into two jagged branches, each continuing downward.
pc.fail: The bolt is a perfectly straight beam or a smooth curve; or a wide glowing tube; or the two branches have no trunk and start separately from the cloud; or the branches cross or rejoin below the fork; or a branch turns and climbs back upward.

pc.expect: The whole bolt, trunk and both branches, appears and vanishes together within a moment, perhaps flickering; the sky returns to dark.
pc.fail: One branch appears after the other has vanished; or the bolt stands as a steady lit line for the rest of the clip; or the bolt grows slowly like a line being drawn; or one branch remains lit after the rest is gone.

pc.expect: The flash lights the ground beneath both branches and the cloud underside during the bolt.
pc.fail: The bolt is visible while the ground and cloud stay as dark as before; or the ground is lit under one branch only while the other branch is as bright; or the ground lights up while no bolt is present.

pc.expect: The ground, trees and structures below stay still through the flash; only the light changes.
pc.fail: Trees or structures shift at the flash; or the horizon tilts; or objects on the ground jump between dark and lit frames.

pc.expect: The landscape below is the same before and after the flash; the flash reveals what was there.
pc.fail: Trees or structures appear or vanish between dark and lit frames; or the landscape changes layout; or a bolt hangs frozen in the sky after the flash; or a glowing pillar stands where a branch struck.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The sky's night colour and the ground's colour are consistent before and after the flash.
pc.fail: The sky turns to daylight after the flash; or the ground changes colour; or the cloud changes colour permanently.
